agent_priors_used: PRIOR (agent knowledge, NOT SPIDER evidence): small-model tool-use failure is frequently instruction or context underspecification rather than model incapability; a capability verdict is only valid after controlling prompt quality. Used to justify Intel's prompt-specification separation test rather than a fourth benchmark attempt.

PRIOR (agent knowledge, NOT SPIDER evidence): comparisons between a treatment and baselines that both sit at a performance ceiling carry no information; a pre-execution non-degenerate-range certificate must precede expensive execution. SPIDER's own EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440 is the experimental instance; the general principle is the prior.

PRIOR (agent knowledge, NOT SPIDER evidence): when repeated measurement-invalid packets share one root cause (e.g., unsatisfiable code-hash freeze, volatile header in a response fingerprint), the correct action is a one-time substrate/control-plane repair or an explicit park, not per-experiment rediscovery of the same absence.

PRIOR (agent knowledge, NOT SPIDER evidence): local concentration on a single claim across many cycles is a diagnostic cue to perform a cognitive reset, not a quota forcing a pivot (exploration/exploitation balance). Applied to Physics (C-WEB-DYNAMICS 8/10) and Runtime (C-MEAS-VALID streak 68).

PRIOR (agent knowledge, NOT SPIDER evidence): path dependence and sunk cost — an already-frozen experiment is completed before strategic redirection because its design is committed and its marginal cost is low relative to its decision value; only pre-freeze work may be superseded.

allocation.question: On a stdlib-only locally served multi-endpoint multi-verb HTTP application whose goal texts are authored by a process that never sees the mechanism intent strings, with a preregistered contamination screen measuring every goal's overlap against EVERY registry intent (not only its own family), a preregistered authoring-provenance record, a reference arm provably distinct from the candidate (the prior argmax-w*cos+b arm was provably identical to the candidate), and positive/null/dynamic-range controls each arithmetically able to fail and live-verified before freeze: does max-cosine-similarity selection over intent embeddings still bind the correct mechanism on goals never seen at authoring time, and by how much does it exceed a token-overlap null on those same independently authored goals - i.e., does the bounded 45/52 vs 33/52 advantage (paired family-blocked difference 0.2308, 95% CI [0.1136, 0.3509]) survive removal of the joint-authorship confound, or was it an artifact of intents and goal templates authored in the same execute-time file by the same agent, with abstention scored as its own class, pooled false-accept <= 0.10, UNKNOWN precision >= 0.85 and ECE <= 0.15 (bootstrap upper <= 0.18)?
allocation.rationale: The graph lane's inherited handoff (four-anchor D1V C-FRESHNESS population) has produced a decisive feasibility verdict: the transport-value coupling is time-stable but the D1V population is single-anchor, so the four-anchor Part II route is parked on accepted evidence (EXP-GRAPH-37992949248) and re-running it would be a pointless repetition. Cognitive reset: with today's Codex, the highest-value graph question is C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE because semantic addressing (goal to applicable mechanism without internal ids) is the user-facing core of the product, and it is the only graph claim carrying a real positive signal (45/52 embedding selection over 33/52 lexical) whose validity is indeterminate solely because of a removable joint-authorship confound plus six individually fixable instrument defects. A discriminating re-test can upgrade or retire that signal; a null result on independently authored goals would be a clean, decision-changing negative. The repeated prior MEASUREMENT_INVALIDs on this claim were all driven by the V9 code-hash control-plane defect and tautological arms, which design-contract v2 (freeze_artifacts_bound) and the mandate's explicit reference-arm-distinctness requirement neutralize rather than rediscover. Pivoting graph back to C-FRESHNESS or onto C-DELTA-REPAIR would be lower leverage: C-DELTA-REPAIR's next gate requires an expensive distributed n>=800 real-LLM-authorization substrate whose marginal value is below this near-free decisive semantics test.
